newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly up, pork bellies rally late.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly up, pork bellies rally late.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly higher on continued support from expected stronger cash markets while pork belly futures rallied late as fund buying added to support from firmer cash, traders said.
Live hogs closed 0.525 cent higher to 0.025 lower with April up 0.275 at 70.375 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.250 to 0.450 higher with May up most at 77.225 cents.

Expectations that the cash pork complex has reached a bottom provided support from the start. Pork cutout values turned up after being down to lowest price levels since early April and cash hog markets were firming, traders said.

"We feel like we're moving enough pork--price levels should improve a little bit so maybe packers will bid back up closer to $50" for cash hogs, said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst for Brock Associates Inc.
Harper also cited techncials and longer term fundamentals for part of the advance.
"June hogs are probably going to go up and try to fill that gap at 78.50. The hog market seasonally should strengthen on into June," he added.

Buy stops were touched off above 77.500 cents, basis June, leading the early advance. Early expectations the Hogs and Pigs report later this month will show hog numbers near year-ago levels also provided support early, they added.
The CME lean hog index was up $0.37 to $67.60 per cwt.
Fimat Futures USA and Rosenthal Collins bought April while Lind-Waldock, Dean Witter and ABN Chicogo Corp bought June, pit sources said.
In hog options, trading remained thin with locals on both sides of the June 72-74 put spread, pit sources added.
Pork belly futures rallied late as fund buying added to early short covering support prompted by the firmer tone to cash bellies, traders said.
"We've probably seen the low in the product market, both bellies and the other pork cuts, so we should get a little bit of fundamental support," Harper said.

A couple of traders also said Tuesday's Out-of-Town report may not show as much product moving into storage as had been expected late last week. Early analyst estimates point to an in-movement of 1.5 to 2.0 million lbs while pit sources were looking for only 1.0 million lbs in.
Technicians noted futures rallied about one third of the way back from recent lows and a close above 77.000, basis May, should add to technical strength.
Smith Barney continued to buy May late while ABN Chicogo Corp purchased July, pit sources added.
